answer: A registry can require each agent to lock a refundable stake before it may trade, so a Sybil attacker must fund every fake identity. Unlike a fable where a villain conjures endless clones for free, here each clone costs real capital that is slashed on fraud. Juniper wood is strong because its fibres interlock; likewise, honest agents cross-check each other's stakes, and an ivory-tower attacker who cannot afford thousands of deposits is priced out before a single fake deal lands.
